findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the behavioral-fidelity spec to state that the space-separated following-token '--force <reason>' form applies to CLAIM ONLY (per claim.py `_parse_force`) and that transition's '--force' takes a reason ONLY via '=' (per transition.py `_parse_flags` and test_force_does_not_swallow_a_following_token); drop 'preserve identically on claim AND transition' for the following-token rule.
evidence: Plan text: 'bare --force consumes the FOLLOWING token as reason only if it does not start with --, else the default note. Preserve identically on claim AND transition.'
claim.py L44-46: `if a == "--force": nxt = args[i+1] ...; return nxt if nxt and not nxt.startswith("--") else "(no reason given)"` — claim DOES consume the following token.
transition.py L175-177: `elif a == "--force": force_reason = ""; i += 1` — transition does NOT consume the following token.

tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py::test_force_does_not_swallow_a_following_token (L60-72) asserts `_parse_flags(["--force", "--class=regression"])` yields force_reason=='' and close_class=='regression', and its docstring: '`--force` takes its reason ONLY via `=`, never as the next argv token.'
findings.finding: The behavioral-fidelity assertion that bare '--force' consumes a FOLLOWING non-'--' token as its reason and that this must be 'Preserve[d] identically on claim AND transition' is refuted by the code: claim's _parse_force consumes the following token, but transition's _parse_flags does NOT (it only reads a reason via '--force=') and a direct-caller test pins that difference.
findings.location: Approach > Behavioral fidelity, bullet '--force accepts --force=<reason> AND space-separated --force <reason>' ('Preserve identically on claim AND transition')
scenarios: Refactoring transition's argparse parser to make bare '--force' consume a following non-'--' token (to match claim) would flip observable behavior and break test_force_does_not_swallow_a_following_token, which the plan lists as a must-pass-unchanged direct-caller test.
An operator running `transition <id> closed --force --class=regression` would have --class swallowed as the force reason under the 'identical' rule, causing a spurious missing-class failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the bullet: for claim, bare '--force' consumes the next token iff it does not start with '--' else '(no reason given)'; for transition, '--force' never consumes a following token (reason only via '--force=<reason>'), bare '--force' -> ''/'(no reason given)'. This matches the two current implementations and keeps test_force_does_not_swallow_a_following_token passing.

evidence: Plan: 'bare --force consumes the FOLLOWING token as reason only if it does not start with --, else the default note. Preserve identically on claim AND transition.'
src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:175-180 — `elif a == "--force": force_reason = ""` (bare force, no following-token consumption)
src/rebar/_commands/claim.py:44-46 — claim's `--force` DOES consume the next non-`--` token
Testing section promises test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py passes unchanged
findings.finding: The Behavioral-fidelity `--force` bullet conflates two DIFFERENT hand-loop behaviors and instructs the implementer to preserve claim's following-token rule 'identically on claim AND transition', but transition._parse_flags never consumes a following token for `--force` (bare `--force` -> force_reason=""), whereas claim._parse_force does. Following the instruction would change transition's observable parsing and break the promised-unchanged test.
findings.location: Approach > Behavioral fidelity, the `--force accepts ...` bullet
scenarios: `ticket transition abc1 closed --force --class=regression`: under the plan's stated rule transition would treat this differently than today (today: bare force + class=regression)
The shim's 5-tuple contract (force_reason=='', close_class=='regression') would change, failing test_force_does_not_swallow_a_following_token
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the bullet to distinguish the two commands: (a) claim `_parse_force` — `--force=<x>`->x (empty->'(no reason given)'), bare `--force`-> next non-`--` token else '(no reason given)'; (b) transition `_parse_flags` — `--force=<x>`->x (incl. empty->''), bare `--force`->'' and MUST NOT consume the following token. Drop 'Preserve identically on claim AND transition' for the following-token guard.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC1's argparse-generated --help with the existing dispatch-layer golden-help mechanism (_help.subcommand_help + src/rebar/_cli/help/{claim,transition}.txt): confirm whether an in-command format_help() path is reachable/needed at all, and if kept, ensure it does not diverge from the byte-exact goldens pinned by test_schema_coverage / test_force_unification_blusterous / test_review_flags.
evidence: Golden help files already exist: src/rebar/_cli/help/claim.txt and transition.txt are present among 55 pinned .txt files.

--help/-h for a subcommand is intercepted at the DISPATCH layer BEFORE the handler: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:701-702 'if rest and rest[0] in ("--help", "-h") ... return _emit_subcommand_help(sub)', which prints the golden text (line 251 sys.stdout.write(text)).

Live contracts pin the golden text, NOT argparse output: tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py:64, tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_force_unification_blusterous.py:131, tests/unit/test_review_flags.py:363 all read _help.subcommand_help(...)/claim.txt.
NIH: the plan rebuilds help rendering that _help.py already provides; golden-hammer: argparse's format_help() is forced where a curated byte-exact contract exists.

The plan is declared 'behavior-preserving MECHANICAL adapter refactor', but parser.format_help() output is not byte-identical to the curated goldens, so an in-command format_help() path would change observable --help output.
findings.finding: AC1 proposes generating claim/transition --help from argparse flag definitions via parser.format_help(), which rebuilds the existing byte-exact golden help mechanism (src/rebar/_cli/help/<sub>.txt via _help.subcommand_help) and forces argparse's help generator onto a surface that already has a curated, test-pinned help contract.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC1; 'Behavioral fidelity' section ('the command detects -h/--help ... prints parser.format_help()')
scenarios: A reviewer runs `rebar claim --help`: today it prints the byte-exact claim.txt golden via dispatch; the in-command format_help() detector is never reached for this path, making it dead code.
If the in-command detector IS reached (e.g. `rebar claim <id> --help`), it emits argparse-generated text that diverges from the pinned golden, breaking the 'behavior-preserving' guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the in-command format_help() detector and rely on the existing dispatch-layer --help interception (_cli/__init__.py) that already renders the pinned golden claim.txt/transition.txt; if AC1's 'help generated from flag definitions' is truly wanted, make it a separate, explicitly-scoped change that regenerates the golden .txt files (keeping them the single source of truth) rather than adding a parallel argparse help path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the claim._parse_force/_parse_assignee caller inventory via find_referencing_symbols (structural refs) AND a string-name grep sweep (monkeypatch.setattr/getattr/importlib), rather than grep alone, before relying on 'no external direct callers'.
evidence: Plan text: "claim's `_parse_force`/`_parse_assignee` have no external direct callers (grep-verified) and may be replaced freely"
grep sweep confirms only internal callers (claim.py:292, claim.py:296) — result complete, but derivation method (grep) is the flagged defect per the stated-method branch
findings.finding: The claim that claim._parse_force/_parse_assignee have 'no external direct callers' is derived via '(grep-verified)', a positively-stated hand-enumeration method. Serena's find_referencing_symbols was not used. The result happens to be correct (only internal claim.py callers at lines 292/296 exist), but grep-only derivation would silently miss string-based or dynamic references (e.g. monkeypatch.setattr, getattr, importlib) that the LSP surfaces and grep-for-the-name may not attribute to these functions.
findings.location: Preserving direct callers section: 'claim's `_parse_force`/`_parse_assignee` have no external direct callers (grep-verified) and may be replaced freely'
scenarios: A future or existing string-based reference to _parse_force/_parse_assignee (e.g. via monkeypatch.setattr(claim, '_parse_force', ...) or getattr) would not be structurally caught by grep-for-the-name and would break silently after the functions are replaced.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace '(grep-verified)' with a note that find_referencing_symbols returned no structural references and a string-name sweep found no dynamic references outside claim.py.
